items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: We would go to Rochester and hear Joe Romano and Chuck Mangione and Don Menza.

ctx.x: In today’s — well generally, who do you think is the main timekeeper in a combo?

I’ve always felt that that was everybody’s responsibility to play the time. The musicians that I grew up with, and that I grew up listening to, my brothers and I will say the same thing. We would go to Rochester and hear Joe Romano and Chuck Mangione and Don Menza. Those guys could stand on the stage and play without anybody and you feel that time, you know, rock solid. So that’s what I expect from all musicians. They don’t have to play it exactly the same feel that maybe I’m used to, but as long as they’re…

This may expose my musical tastes but it seems like I hear a lot of contemporary groups now where most people are playing with the time, instead of playing the time. And I wonder if you’ve noticed that kind of thing, maybe in a different fashion, but it almost feels like they’re avoiding being too obvious.
